prompt_md: A help centre writes article vectors in the order `[delivery, money, fixing a problem]` (1 = yes, 0 = no). Which article is `[0, 1, 1]`?

options.why_md: Right. Not about delivery (0), about money (1), and a problem to fix (1).
That is about delivery and a problem to fix: `[1, 0, 1]` in this order.
About money, but a how-to guide rather than a problem: `[0, 1, 0]`.

hints: Read each position with this list's order, which starts with *delivery*.
Position 1 (delivery) = 0, position 2 (money) = 1, position 3 (fixing a problem) = 1. Which article is about money and is a complaint?
solution_md: In the order `[delivery, money, fixing a problem]`, `[0, 1, 1]` means: not delivery, about money, fixing a problem. That is *Why was I charged twice?*. Reading it in some other order would give a different answer, which is why the order is part of the vector.

prompt_md:
**Assertion (A):** With one-hot vectors, *cancel* and *unsubscribe* share 0 features, even though they mean nearly the same.

**Reason (R):** A one-hot vector has a single 1, in its own word's slot, so two different words never have a 1 in the same position.

options.why_md: Right. A is true, and R is exactly why: with the 1s in different slots, no position has a 1 in both.

options.md: Both true; R does not explain A
options.why_md: R is the direct cause of A: sharing a feature needs a position where both are 1, and R rules that out.
R is the definition of a one-hot vector, so it is true.
A follows from R: meaning-alike words get 0 shared features in one-hot, like every other pair of different words.

hints: Check A and R separately, then ask whether R is the reason A happens.
R is the definition of one-hot. If two words never have a 1 in the same position, how many features can they share?
solution_md: R is the definition of one-hot, so it is true. It forces A: two different words have their 1s in different slots, so they share 0 features, whatever they mean. Both are true and R explains A: **a**.

prompt_md: The support team wants a **Similar complaints** view in which articles about something going wrong sit together, whatever their subject (payments, parcels, sign-in). Which feature list should describe the articles?

options.why_md: These group by subject. *Why was I charged twice?* would sit with *Change your billing card*, a how-to guide, rather than with other complaints.
Right. Every complaint has a 1 for *fixing a problem*, whatever its subject, so complaints share a feature and sit together.
Every pair of different articles shares 0 features, so nothing would sit together.

options.md: `[word count in thousands, days since last update]`
options.why_md: These group articles by length and age, which says nothing about whether something went wrong.

hints: Name the property every article in the view should have in common, then find the list that has it as a feature.
The shared property is “something went wrong”. Which list includes *fixing a problem*?
solution_md: The view should group by “something went wrong”, regardless of subject. Only `[how-to steps, fixing a problem]` has that as a feature, so complaints share it and land together. The topic list groups by subject, one-hot groups nothing, and length/age features group by the wrong thing. **b**.

prompt_md:
Four articles under two feature lists:

| | topic `[money, sign-in, delivery]` | task `[how-to steps, fixing a problem]` |
|---|---|---|
| *Download your invoice* | `[1, 0, 0]` | `[1, 0]` |
| *Why was I charged twice?* | `[1, 0, 0]` | `[0, 1]` |
| *Turn on two-step sign-in* | `[0, 1, 0]` | `[1, 0]` |
| *My parcel arrived damaged* | `[0, 0, 1]` | `[0, 1]` |

A third option is one-hot, with one slot per article. Match each feature list to what it ranks nearest to *Download your invoice* by shared features.

options.why_md: Invoice `[1, 0, 0]` shares *money* with charged twice and nothing with the others.
Invoice `[1, 0]` shares *how-to steps* with two-step sign-in and nothing with the others.
Every pair of different articles shares 0 features.
Nearest under the topic list: 1 shared feature (money) against 0 and 0.
Nearest under the task list: both are how-to guides, 1 shared feature against 0 and 0.

options.md: No single article: the other three tie at 0
options.why_md: This is what one-hot gives: no two different articles share a 1.
It shares 0 features with the invoice under both lists, so no list puts it first.

hints: For each list, count the features each article shares with the invoice and pick the highest.
Topic: invoice `[1, 0, 0]` shares 1 only with charged twice. Task: invoice `[1, 0]` shares 1 only with two-step sign-in. One-hot: 0 with everyone.
solution_md: Topic list: invoice shares 1 with *Why was I charged twice?* (money) and 0 with the rest → r1. Task list: invoice shares 1 with *Turn on two-step sign-in* (how-to steps) and 0 with the rest → r2. One-hot: all three share 0 → r3. *My parcel arrived damaged* is never nearest.
